description: During the live Amazing Race event, David reported three dashboard defects in one sweep: (1) clicking Approve on a flag scored 0 points instead of the post's full quest value — approve was implemented as rubber-stamping the vision verdict's suggested_points, which is 0 for review/fail verdicts; (2) unidentified posts had no action buttons at all; (3) the Reject button did nothing. Root cause of (3): a broken edit to apply_ruling.py (dangling def with no body) crashed the dashboard daemon's import at restart, leaving it down. Follow-up: the real root cause of dead buttons was JS scope — rule() and classify() were defined inside tick()'s closure, so the buttons' onclick handlers (which execute in global scope) could not resolve them; every click silently threw ReferenceError. The daemon outage was a second, overlapping cause.
correction: Approve now awards the quest's full value (full_quest_points: fixed points, or per-item points x matched items, full item list when the reviewer could not confirm, capped at base_item_cap) computed at ruling time. Unidentified posts get team/quest number inputs plus a Classify & score full points button (POST /api/classify rewrites posts.jsonl, updates or creates the flag, applies an ok ruling at full points). Every script edit mid-event is now compile-checked before daemon restart.
systemic_fix: apply_ruling.py (full_quest_points + apply ok-path uses ruled_points) and dashboard_server.py (POST /api/classify + classify UI + JS) updated; scoring.py honors ruled_points for ok rulings. Ruling semantics codified: approve = post counts fully regardless of vision verdict; override = explicit points; reject = 0. Fixed: rule/classify moved to global scope in the dashboard page template; additionally, per David's rule, Approve never offers 0 — quest is inferred from the post caption (guess_quest keyword table from quest titles) when the number is missing, and the approve_points label shows the value an Approve will award.
